While the story is well-written and evocative, it explores very familiar and conventional literary themes: returning to a childhood home after the death of a parent, the triggering of grief and memory through sensory details (the smell of the rose hand cream), and the realization that while physical spaces remain static, it is the people who change over time. Although these themes are emotionally resonant, they do not present a unique or original idea to the average reader.
